one_liner: Tiny Grisu2 C library converting doubles to shortest round-trip strings, ~10x faster than std::ostringstream.
what_it_does: fpconv solves double-to-ASCII conversion: it emits the shortest decimal string that round-trips back to the original IEEE-754 double, without going through locale-aware formatted I/O. The whole API is one function, `int fpconv_dtoa(double fp, char dest[24])`, which writes into a caller-supplied 24-byte buffer and returns the character count. Output is not null-terminated and the call signature is nothing like `ostringstream`, `sprintf`, or `std::to_chars`, so call sites need to be rewritten, not swapped in.
how_it_is_fast: Implements Fabian Loitsch's Grisu2 algorithm: the double's mantissa/exponent are converted to a 64-bit fixed-point `Fp` struct, scaled into a normalized range using a precomputed table of 87 power-of-ten cache constants (powers.h), and digits are generated directly via integer division against upper/lower boundary intervals (`generate_digits`/`round_digit`). This avoids the arbitrary-precision bignum arithmetic and locale/format-flag machinery that `sprintf`/`ostringstream` pay for, at the cost of Grisu2 occasionally emitting one digit more than the true shortest form (unlike Grisu3/Ryu, which always find the minimal digit count).
when_to_use: Hot-path double serialization (JSON/log/wire-format emitters) where sprintf/ostringstream formatting overhead shows up in profiles
C or C++ code that can vendor a single .c/.h pair rather than pull in a library or link a header-only C++ template
Need the shortest round-trippable string and don't care about scientific/fixed formatting control
Embedded or size-constrained builds where a ~300-line, dependency-free source drop is preferable to a bigger conversion library
when_not_to_use: Need std::to_chars/from_chars-compatible API, or sprintf-style format control (precision, fixed vs scientific) - fpconv only emits shortest round-trip form
Need string-to-double parsing too - fpconv is dtoa-only, no strtod-equivalent shipped
Want active upstream maintenance - repo is stale (last commit Dec 2023), single maintainer, tiny community (62 stars, 14 forks)

Vendoring an old/pinned copy predating the Dec 2023 fix: versions before that had a documented 24-byte buffer overflow on some large-magnitude doubles (e.g. -2^77), overflowing the buffer the header itself recommends
Want benchmark evidence against a modern baseline - the only published numbers are vs VC2013 ostringstream/sprintf on a 2009 Core i7-920, not vs std::to_chars

integration.dependencies: none (only C stdlib headers: stdbool.h, string.h, stdint.h)
integration.min_toolchain: not documented; plain C99 (uses stdbool.h/stdint.h), no CMake or version pin in the repo
integration.platforms: any platform with IEEE-754 doubles; pure C with no SIMD/intrinsics, bit access via a union type-pun
integration.thread_safety: not documented, but appears reentrant: fpconv.c and powers.h contain no mutable global/static state, only a read-only power-of-ten table and stack locals
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — different function signature than std::to_string/ostringstream/sprintf, caller must adapt the call site, and the output buffer is not null-terminated

gotchas: Pre-Dec-2023 snapshots overflow the documented 24-byte buffer for some large-magnitude values (GitHub issue #5, e.g. -2^77); fixed in the same commit recorded as last_commit (2023-12-14), so only affects older vendored copies
Output is not null-terminated; caller must track and use the returned length
Grisu2 can emit one extra digit versus the true shortest representation in rare cases (no Grisu3/Ryu fallback)
Repo also bundles an unmaintained D port (fpconv_ctfe.d); it is not covered by the same fix history as the C code
pick_this_over_siblings_when: On the same dtoa-benchmark page, both milo Grisu2 (138.021ns) and google/double-conversion (201.645ns) beat fpconv (273.822ns) outright, so pick this over them only when you specifically want a minimal plain-C .c/.h pair to vendor rather than a header-only C++ template (milo) or a heavier C++ library with a bignum fallback path (double-conversion); pick Boost.Charconv, c4core, or rigtorp/CharConv instead if you want a std::to_chars-shaped API.
verified_claims_summary: On the independent miloyip/dtoa-benchmark RandomDigit case (1,000 random doubles, 1-17 significant digits, min of 10 trials x100 iterations), fpconv converts in 273.822ns vs sprintf's 1,256.376ns (4.59x) and std::ostringstream's 2,778.748ns (~10.1x, derived), measured with MSVC 2013 on Windows x64 on a Core i7-920 @2.67GHz.
status_note: Stale since its last commit in December 2023 (which was also the fix for the buffer-overflow bug) with a small community (62 stars, 14 forks), but it's a two-file BSL-1.0 source drop small enough to read end-to-end and vendor with confidence.
